findings.summary: the surface-parity assertion compares a registry against itself
findings.text: test_the_tool_and_the_dispatcher_declare_the_same_views compares mcp.CREW_TOOL_VIEWS against mcp_views.crew_view_names(); reckon/mcp.py:235 assigns CREW_TOOL_VIEWS = CREW_VIEWS and reckon/mcp_views.py:3623 has crew_view_names return the same CREW_VIEWS tuple, so both sides are one object and the assertion holds whatever serve_crew_view does. It cannot catch the one-surface-only drift its docstring claims, and only the declared monkeypatch makes it fail, so the parity of the declared surface rests on the mutation.

findings.summary: the document-parity case drives only one argument vector
findings.text: _READ_ARGUMENTS is the single vector (project, since, until) both surfaces are driven with, so the parity case never exercises the CLI's --fields, --source, --scope, --candidates or --pretty plumbing; a regression that dropped any of those options from reckon/crew_run_commands.py:365 crew_view would leave the comparison green because neither side is asked for them.

findings.summary: a changed file is absent from the manifest's changed_paths
findings.text: The diff changes this file to add the ("crew", "view") flag-map row, but the manifest's changed_paths and orientation_write_paths list neither it nor any other entry for it, so a coordinator reading the manifest cannot see that this file was touched; the review found it only by reading the diff.

item_verdicts.diff: Read commit by commit against the base sha 9c353762e; five commits change eight files, moving the view dispatch into reckon/mcp_views.py, adding the crew view verb, the parity test and the evidence fragment, all inside the fence.
item_verdicts.done_when: The done_when names tests/test_crew_view_serves_every_view.py, the tombstone exit code, the caller census and the negative control; the worker's gate runs that file and records 1 failed/91 passed at the head with zero added failures over the base arm, and the census is accurate, but no tombstone clause is exercised because no verb was retired.
item_verdicts.goal: The node goal is to serve every crew MCP view through one function both the tool and a crew view CLI verb call and to retire the five read verbs to tombstones once no tracked caller remains; reckon/mcp_views.py:3626 serve_crew_view plus reckon/crew_run_commands.py:365 crew_view and reckon/mcp.py:1998 deliver the first half, and the second is correctly withheld because callers remain.
item_verdicts.manifest: Read; it declares five commits, the gate command and logs, a caller census, five follow-ons for the un-retired verbs, and a negative-control note; its changed_paths omits tests/test_skill_contracts.py and it names no ruff log for the ruff sub-claim.
item_verdicts.write_paths: The declared fence is the plan's write set plus a documented mid-run extension to tests/test_skill_contracts.py; every path in the diff is inside it, though tests/test_skill_contracts.py is absent from the manifest's own changed_paths.

justifications.durability: the document-parity case at tests/test_crew_view_serves_every_view.py:213 drives both surfaces through real code, but the name-parity case at line 154 compares two references to the same CREW_VIEWS tuple and the parity case drives only one argument vector.
justifications.evidence: base-arm.log and gate-head-2.log record the gate and both arms with EXIT lines and zero added failures, but the tombstone clause is unexercised and the ruff sub-claim in the evidence fragment rests on no cited log, the only ruff log on disk (ruff.log) being a stale pre-fix artifact showing an F401 at reckon/mcp.py:56 that does not exist at head.
justifications.fit: the added symbols (CREW_VIEWS, serve_crew_view, crew_view) name the capability they carry with no plan or ticket reference and match the surrounding style of reckon/mcp_views.py, though the invalid_view refusal text is duplicated verbatim at reckon/mcp.py:1984 and reckon/mcp_views.py:3719.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/mcp_views.py:3626 serve_crew_view is the one function both reckon/mcp.py:1998 and reckon/crew_run_commands.py:416 call, so every view is served through one implementation; the five read verbs stay visible only because tracked callers of theirs remain, verified at reckon/mcp_deadlines.py:184.
justifications.reuse: serve_crew_view relocates the tool's inline view dispatch rather than adding a parallel one, and a capability search over reckon/ found no pre-existing owner of a crew-view registry, so the added registry and dispatcher are the first.
justifications.scope_discipline: every changed file lies inside the fence as extended mid-run, but the manifest's changed_paths and orientation_write_paths omit tests/test_skill_contracts.py, which the diff changes at line 1287.
